newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY MHB TO START NEW INSURANCE DIVISION.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY MHB TO START NEW INSURANCE DIVISION.

text.p: Hungary's Magyar Hitel Bank said on Wednesday it hopes to leap to a leading position in the insurance market with a new division that will start operations in late April or early May.

"We plan to increase our capital to 7.5 billion forints during the next few years from the present 2.15 billion," Bela Horvath, general manager of MHB's new subsidiary, Magyar Elet- es Nyugdijbiztosito (MEBIT), told Reuters.
Dutch banking group ABN AMRO in December acquired an 89.23 percent stake in MHB for $89.23 million and announced plans to invest a further $137 million in the bank.
Horvath, speaking after a news conference, said that MEBIT plans to build on the expansion potential of the domestic market rather than taking away customers from other insurance companies.
"The Hungarian insurance market has a roughly sevenfold growth potential," Horvath said.
Istvan Komoroczki, MHB's public relations director, said that during the privatisation talks MHB's plans to set up an insurance company were seen as a boon by ABN AMRO.
"One of ABN AMRO's major competitors, Nationale-Nederlanden, already has an insurance company in Hungary," he said.
He added that MHB originally planned to set up the insurance company jointly with financial investors, but the sale of the bank to a strong group changed that.
"We can now do it on our own," he said. Horvath added that ABN AMRO fully backs the expansion plans that envisage MEBIT turning profitable in four to five years.
"We have high ambitions but nothing presses us," he said. "We have a very serious capital backing us up". He also said MEBIT will have an exclusive offer of insurance products on the domestic market.
"We have acquired exclusive rights from abroad for some products that no other insurance company will offer to domestic customers," he said, but did not give details.
An official of Concorde Securities, the company commissioned last summer by MHB to do a feasability study, said MEBIT's plans for strong marketing will be an advantage in the Hungarian market.
"There is hardly any competitor on the domestic scene who can keep its existing market share when faced with aggressive marketing activity," Gyorgy Jaksity, Concorde's managing director said.
